title: Guard and close-phase accept a proven merge commit (D110 part 1, D113(1))
scope:
**Read FIRST and follow exactly:** the campaign brief `.shipwright/planning/campaigns/2026-11-27-dfp-changelog-followups-BRIEF.md` (this unit in section 1, golden freeze section 2, how each unit runs section 3, operator decisions section 5) and FINDINGS rows D110 and D113 in `.shipwright/planning/campaigns/2026-10-25-dfp-pilot-changelog-FINDINGS.md`. **Goal.** The release record gains optional `published_commit`, `merged_via` and a proof block. A new stdlib-only `scripts/hooks/release_merge_proof.py` holds the one rule the guard and close-phase use (the release descent, or `published_commit` whose tree still equals the recorded tree). `tag_local`, `tag_remote` and `pr_state` accept it; the closing summary reads the real tag state (D113(1)). Inert until U3 writes the fields.

- [ ] The second close-phase summary says pushed once the tag is on origin

title: push-tag after a squash or rebase merge: proof, retag, record, stop on foreign commits (D110 part 2, D112)
scope:
**Read FIRST and follow exactly:** the campaign brief `.shipwright/planning/campaigns/2026-11-27-dfp-changelog-followups-BRIEF.md` (this unit in section 1, golden freeze section 2, how each unit runs section 3, operator decisions section 5) and FINDINGS rows D110 and D112 in `.shipwright/planning/campaigns/2026-10-25-dfp-pilot-changelog-FINDINGS.md`. Anything that needs an operator answer is a STRICT-STOP.

**Goal.** `release.py push-tag` accepts the merge commit only when the PR head is the release commit (or an event-only descendant), the merge commit is on the freshly fetched base, and both trees are equal. Nothing weaker. Otherwise stop with `foreign_commits_on_base`, naming the commits and their pending drops, and tag nothing. On success write the proof into the record, retag in code only when the tag is not on origin, return the tag push line; idempotent re-run. A merge commit keeps today's path (tag the release commit).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] L1 end to end (real git, bare remote, gh stub with mergeCommit): squash merge, push-tag, tag push through the guard, close-phase 8 of 8
- [ ] The same with a rebase merge, and with a merge commit (tag on the release commit)
- [ ] A foreign commit merged before the squash ends in `foreign_commits_on_base` naming it and its drop; tags and record unchanged
- [ ] A re-run gives the same answer; a tag already on origin is never moved

title: Autonomous merge: pick the method, pin the head, stop when behind
scope:
**Read FIRST and follow exactly:** the campaign brief `.shipwright/planning/campaigns/2026-11-27-dfp-changelog-followups-BRIEF.md` (this unit in section 1, golden freeze section 2, how each unit runs section 3, operator decisions section 5). Anything that needs an operator answer is a STRICT-STOP.

**Goal.** The autonomous merge picks the method from the repo settings (merge commit preferred), always passes `--match-head-commit`, and before a squash or rebase merge stops when the base moved: the release must be restarted (operator decision, no automatic rebuild). The merge stays one literal outward line in SKILL.md; a release.py call answers which line to run. Guided mode text: merge while the branch is up to date.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Squash-only repo: a squash line with `--match-head-commit`; merge commits allowed: `--merge`
- [ ] A moved base stops with a plain restart message and nothing is merged
- [ ] The guard allows the chosen line during a release

title: Pipeline: a phase can wait for the release PR merge (shipwright-run)
scope:
**Read FIRST and follow exactly:** the campaign brief `.shipwright/planning/campaigns/2026-11-27-dfp-changelog-followups-BRIEF.md` (this unit in section 1, how each unit runs section 3, operator decisions section 5) and `docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md`. Requirement FR-01.01. Anything that needs an operator answer is a STRICT-STOP, and a needed new value in `shared/schemas/run_config.v2.schema.json` is one.

**Goal.** A phase result can say it waits for an outside event (`waiting_for_merge`, with the PR URL). The single-session loop then answers a waiting action: no new dispatch, nothing failed, run not complete, deploy not scheduled; the resume card says what to do. On resume the same changelog task is dispatched again. Inert until U6 emits the result.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A waiting changelog result leaves the task not done, the run not complete and deploy not scheduled
- [ ] The loop reports the waiting action with the PR URL; on resume the changelog task is dispatched again
- [ ] A second result ok moves on to deploy, or ends the run with deploy_target none
- [ ] Every current shipwright-run test stays green
